transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I came in because I’m kind of… stuck on this thing with my face, and I know that probably sounds strange. It’s mostly the left side. I keep feeling like it looks uneven and puffy, especially on video calls for work or in photos from salsa nights. Like, I’ll see myself on screen and I can’t stop looking at that side of my face instead of paying attention to what people are saying.

Everyone keeps telling me they don’t see what I’m talking about, or that it looks normal, but I can’t seem to let it go. And it’s gotten to the point where it’s starting to affect work and my social life, because I’m distracted and self-conscious, and I’m avoiding things or not enjoying them the way I used to. So… I guess that’s why I’m here.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to check, fix, or reassure yourself about how your face looks, like adjusting your hair, checking mirrors, or seeking reassurance from others?

Yes. I do that a lot, honestly. Before meetings especially, I’ll open the camera preview over and over, even if the meeting hasn’t started yet, and I’ll keep changing the angle of the laptop or moving a lamp or turning toward the window to see if that side of my face looks less… wrong, I guess. I’ll think, “Okay, maybe it’s just the lighting,” but then I adjust it and still stare at it, and then I’m not really calmer.

If I’m going out, it’s similar. I’ll fix my hair around the left side of my face so it kind of covers it, then I’ll move it because it looks obvious, then put it back again. I’ll take pictures to check how I look, but one picture makes me feel worse, so I take another one from a different angle, and then another. It can turn into this whole thing where I’m supposed to be leaving and I’m still in the bathroom or by the mirror, trying to get proof that it’s fine.

And I do ask people. Mostly friends, like before salsa or if we’re taking photos, I’ll ask, “Does my face look weird?” or “Do I look puffy on this side?” And they’ll say no, but then I’ll ask again in a slightly different way, which I know is annoying. Sometimes by the time I’m done checking and fixing everything, I’m late, or I feel so drained and embarrassed that I don’t even want to go anymore.
